statistical_scope: One deterministic trace per configuration; no confidence interval.

analysis_limitations: Path-truth propagation RTT includes both directions; RTT decreases alone do not prove forward-path overtaking.
Repeated cumulative ACKs are observations, not an independent reconstruction of every duplicate-ACK predicate.
Exact tx_id tags, not packet UIDs, identify transmission instances; joins are retained for a bounded time.
Candidate unnecessary recovery associates a sequence gap, ACK evidence, retransmission and eventual original delivery; controlled comparisons are still needed for a causal performance claim.
LOSS state is reported directly and is not automatically called an RTO without a dedicated timer trace.
Drop trace rows can duplicate one physical loss; distinct tagged transmission counts and per-layer counts are separate.
No observed drop is not proof of no drop when coverage or packet parsing is incomplete.
Traffic-control TcDrop coverage is required before excluding network loss; pre-v3 coverage can omit this path.
Root queue-disc absence must be verified per device or explicitly independently audited; TcDrop does not observe a root queue-disc's own losses.
Receiver TCP window rejection and PAWS/input discards are not covered by queue/IP/device/traffic-control hooks.
Pre-processing wire Rx does not prove acceptance: a gap fill requires subsequent expected_seq advancement or same-time application delivery.
Application HandleRead bytes are ordered unique delivery; wire interval union is a separate metric.
Sequence epochs assume adjacent relevant sequence references differ by less than 2^31 bytes.
Static and dynamic path controls, actual loss tests and deployment-information errors remain separate experimental requirements.

finite_size_first_loss.caption: Receiver application completion time from flow start, with exactly one first-segment loss on the stable micro path. Categorical transfer sizes are equally spaced. The exemption bypasses the guard for known total finite length ≤21 MSS. Three-MSS baseline loss also times out; this policy does not solve every short-flow loss. An optional K8 point applies only to the measured 20-MSS case.

finite20_loss_position.caption: Twenty-MSS finite transfer on the stable micro path with one genuine first-, middle- or last-segment loss. Completion is measured at receiver application delivery from flow start. Exemption matches the baseline for first/middle loss but last-segment loss still requires the timeout path in every tested mode.

protection_window_offset.caption: Baseline-relative receiver goodput changes for shifts of both protection-window bounds. Offsets are not notification-arrival times; the physical route event remains at 26.2 s. Every event metric uses the same 25.7–28.2 s analysis window. Both metrics share the same zero-based percentage axis. The 0-ms point is the independently simulated nominal exemption-policy bulk case. Only tested offsets are plotted.

finite_delay_step.caption: Matched 80-MSS finite-transfer completion times from flow start for a stable propagation control and a delay decrease. One-way propagation changes from 50 to 45 ms at 0.201 s in the stepped cases; the control retains 50 ms. Remaining relevant parameters match within each mode, including guard windows. All six cases record zero tagged drops. The known-total-size exemption does not apply at 80 MSS. Values are single deterministic traces, with exact values and parameters in the source manifest.
